tree.name: 1 · Computational methods — what performs the computation?

children.name: Rules and expert systems
children.detail: Explicit rules plus a knowledge base and an inference procedure; forward or backward chaining.

children.name: Logic, theorem proving and program synthesis
children.detail: Deduction, proof search and construction of programs satisfying a specification.

children.name: Ontologies and knowledge graphs
children.detail: Structured entities, relations and axioms; reasoning requires suitable semantics and inference machinery.

children.name: Fuzzy logic
children.detail: Degrees of membership or truth for vague concepts; these are not the same as probabilities.

children.name: Case-based reasoning
children.detail: Retrieve and adapt solutions from similar previous cases.

children.name: State-space and heuristic search
children.detail: Breadth/depth-first search, A*, beam search and related exploration strategies.

children.name: Game-tree and Monte Carlo tree search
children.detail: Minimax, alpha–beta pruning and MCTS; often combined with learned policies or value estimates.

children.name: Constraint solving
children.detail: Constraint satisfaction, SAT/SMT and mathematical optimization; also widely used outside AI.

children.name: Automated and decision-theoretic planning
children.detail: Classical/temporal planning, hierarchical task networks and planning under uncertainty.

children.name: Evolutionary and population methods
children.detail: Genetic algorithms/programming, evolution strategies and swarm methods; not inherently symbolic.

children.name: Bayesian optimization
children.detail: A probabilistic surrogate and acquisition rule guide expensive evaluations; overlaps probabilistic ML.

children.name: Symbolic regression and equation discovery
children.detail: Search for compact mathematical expressions or sparse governing equations that explain observed data.

children.name: Regression and generalized linear models
children.detail: Linear/logistic regression and related regularized predictive models.

children.name: Trees and ensembles
children.detail: Decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, bagging and stacking.

children.name: Kernel and instance-based methods
children.detail: Support vector machines, kernel methods and nearest-neighbour models.

children.name: Clustering and dimensionality reduction
children.detail: k-means, density-based clustering, PCA, manifold methods and matrix factorization.

children.name: Bayesian and graphical models
children.detail: Bayesian networks, Markov models, hidden-state models and probabilistic inference.

children.name: Gaussian processes and probabilistic programming
children.detail: Distributions over functions or programs for inference with explicit uncertainty.

children.name: Structural causal models
children.detail: Represent interventions and causal assumptions; causal conclusions require identification conditions, not correlations alone.

children.name: Feed-forward networks / MLPs
children.detail: Learned compositions of nonlinear transformations; a basic neural architecture.

children.name: Convolutional networks / CNNs
children.detail: Use shared local filters and spatial structure; also apply to time series and other grids.

children.name: Recurrent networks / LSTM / GRU
children.detail: Maintain sequential hidden state for time series, text and other ordered signals.

children.name: Transformers and attention
children.detail: Attention-based sequence/representation architectures; training can parallelize token processing.

children.name: State-space and recurrent–attention hybrids
children.detail: Selective state-space models such as Mamba and mixtures of recurrence with attention.

children.name: Graph neural networks / GNNs
children.detail: Learn from graph structure, often by propagating and aggregating node or edge information.

children.name: Mixture of experts / MoE
children.detail: A router selects expert subnetworks; this is distinct from a team of software agents.

children.name: Spiking and reservoir networks
children.detail: Event-based neurons or fixed recurrent dynamics with trained readouts; specialised and research uses.

children.name: Autoregressive models
children.detail: Generate by conditioning each element on earlier elements; not limited to text or transformers.

children.name: Variational autoencoders / VAEs
children.detail: Latent-variable generation trained with variational inference.

children.name: Generative adversarial networks / GANs
children.detail: Train a generator against a discriminator.

children.name: Diffusion and score-based models
children.detail: Generate through learned reversal of a corruption/noising process.

children.name: Normalizing flows and flow matching
children.detail: Learn transformations or vector fields transporting a base distribution towards data.

children.name: Energy-based models
children.detail: Assign an energy to configurations, with inference or sampling favouring lower-energy states.

children.name: Diffusion language models
children.detail: Iterative token denoising is an alternative to strictly left-to-right language generation.

children.name: State estimation and control — adjacent foundations
State estimation: Kalman and particle filters
children.detail: Infer a changing hidden state from noisy measurements and a dynamics model; a classical foundation adjacent to AI.

children.name: Optimal control and model predictive control
children.detail: Optimize actions through a dynamics model and constraints; MPC repeatedly replans over a moving horizon.

tree.name: 2 · Learning and adaptation — how does behaviour improve?

children.name: Supervised learning
children.detail: Learn from externally supplied target labels or values.

children.name: Unsupervised learning
children.detail: Discover structure or model distributions without externally supplied task labels.

children.name: Semi-supervised learning
children.detail: Combine labelled and unlabelled examples; pseudo-labelling is one possible method.

children.name: Self-supervised learning
children.detail: Derive prediction targets from the data itself, such as masked content, next tokens or paired views.

children.name: Imitation learning
children.detail: Learn behaviour from demonstrations; includes behavioural cloning and interactive variants.

children.name: Model-free ↔ model-based
children.detail: Whether learning/planning uses an explicit environment dynamics model.

children.name: Value-based ↔ policy-based ↔ actor–critic
children.detail: How action values and/or the action-selection policy are represented and optimized.

children.name: Online ↔ offline; on-policy ↔ off-policy
children.detail: Data collection and policy relationships are separate choices, not one exclusive hierarchy.

children.name: Deep RL, hierarchical RL and multi-agent RL
children.detail: Neural function approximation, temporal abstraction and multiple interacting learners.

children.name: Instruction / supervised fine-tuning
children.detail: Adapt a pretrained model using task demonstrations and instruction–response examples.

children.name: RLHF / RLAIF
children.detail: Reinforcement learning from human or AI feedback, often through a learned reward model.

children.name: Preference optimization / DPO
children.detail: Optimize directly from preferences; DPO does not require a separate online RL loop.

children.name: RL with verifiable rewards / RLVR
children.detail: Reward outputs using programmatic checks, such as test results or mathematical answers.

children.name: Transfer learning / domain adaptation / multitask learning
children.detail: Reuse or jointly learn representations across tasks or distributions.

children.name: Active learning
children.detail: Select the examples whose labels are expected to be most useful.

children.name: Meta-learning
children.detail: Learn an initialization, update rule or representation that supports rapid adaptation.

children.name: Online and continual learning
children.detail: Update as data/tasks arrive while managing drift and interference with earlier learning.

children.name: Test-time learning / learned memory
children.detail: Update parameters or learned memory at inference time; distinct from simply spending more compute.

children.name: In-context learning
children.detail: Adapt outputs using examples/context without necessarily updating model weights.

tree.name: 3 · Model roles — what does the model represent or produce?

children.name: Foundation models
children.detail: Broad pretraining with reuse across tasks; can be generative or representation models.

children.name: Task-specific and domain-specialised models
children.detail: Scope/specialisation choices that can overlap foundation-model adaptation.

children.name: Small / edge / compact models
children.detail: Size and deployment properties; not a separate learning paradigm.

children.name: Language models / LLMs
children.detail: Models of language or token sequences; modern examples need not all be autoregressive.

children.name: Vision, audio, video and multimodal models
children.detail: Single-modal or cross-modal inputs/outputs; capabilities need not be symmetric.

children.name: Embedding, ranking and predictive models
children.detail: Produce representations, relevance scores or forecasts rather than generated content.

children.name: Vision–language–action / VLA models
children.detail: Map visual and linguistic context into robot actions; embodied deployment remains task dependent.

children.name: World models
children.detail: Predict environment evolution, often conditioned on actions; can operate in latent, symbolic or observable space.

children.name: Physics-informed and scientific ML
children.detail: Combine learned models with equations, symmetries, physical constraints or numerical solvers.

children.name: Neural operators
children.detail: Learn mappings between functions, for example solution operators for families of physical systems.

children.name: Anomaly and novelty detection
children.detail: Score unusual observations with isolation, density, distance, reconstruction or one-class methods.

tree.name: 4 · System patterns — how are components combined?

children.name: Retrieval-augmented generation / RAG
children.detail: Retrieve external evidence and condition generation on it; retrieval need not use a vector database.

children.name: Graph-augmented and structured retrieval
children.detail: Retrieve over graphs, relations or structured queries; a graph alone does not establish logical reasoning.

children.name: Hybrid retrieval and reranking
children.detail: Combine lexical, vector or structured retrieval and relevance scoring.

children.name: Tool-using agents
children.detail: Select actions, call tools, observe results and continue towards a goal.

children.name: Planning and workflow controllers
children.detail: Use plans, state machines, decomposition, checkpoints and replanning to coordinate work.

children.name: Multi-agent systems
children.detail: Several agents coordinate, negotiate or compete; more agents do not inherently imply better results.

children.name: External memory and episodic retrieval
children.detail: Store/retrieve past events or lessons; no weight update is required.

children.name: Reasoning and computation at inference time
Deliberation and test-time compute
children.detail: Allocate more generation, sampling, search or verification to a problem.

children.name: Self-consistency and candidate search
children.detail: Generate alternatives and use aggregation, search or ranking to select an answer.

children.name: Verifier-guided reasoning
children.detail: Use tests, solvers, proof checkers or other external feedback to evaluate candidates.

children.name: Metacognitive monitoring and control
children.detail: Estimate uncertainty/failure, choose another strategy, gather evidence or abstain; self-critique alone is not verification.

children.name: Neural proposals + symbolic reasoning
children.detail: Neural models propose representations or steps; symbolic engines derive or check consequences.

children.name: Differentiable logic and constrained learning
children.detail: Bring logical or domain constraints into learning objectives or differentiable inference.

children.name: Learning + planning + simulation
children.detail: Combine policies/value models with search and predictive environment models.

children.name: LLMs + evolutionary search + evaluators
children.detail: Generate candidate algorithms, evaluate them and iteratively improve the candidate population.

tree.name: 5 · Cross-cutting engineering — how is it efficient and dependable?

children.name: Distillation / pruning / quantization
children.detail: Transfer behaviour to smaller models, remove parameters or reduce numerical precision.

children.name: Parameter-efficient tuning / LoRA / adapters
children.detail: Adapt a subset or low-rank parameterization instead of updating every weight.

children.name: Federated and privacy-preserving learning
children.detail: Distribute training or protect data/updates; federated learning alone does not guarantee privacy.

children.name: Speculative decoding / caching / routing
children.detail: Improve serving efficiency; these do not constitute new model intelligence by themselves.

children.name: Empirical scaling laws and compute allocation
children.detail: Fit relationships between model size, data, compute and measured performance to guide training experiments.

children.name: Calibration and uncertainty estimation
children.detail: Assess how predictive uncertainty corresponds to observed errors; requires evaluation data.

children.name: Conformal prediction and selective prediction
children.detail: Construct prediction sets under stated assumptions, or abstain on uncertain cases.

children.name: Constraints, validation and formal verification
children.detail: Check specified properties; a proof or validation result is limited by its specification and assumptions.

children.name: Interpretability, provenance and human review
children.detail: Make evidence, behaviour and decision responsibilities inspectable; not proof of correctness.

children.name: Adversarial robustness and AI security
children.detail: Assess deliberate input manipulation and protect model, data and tool trust boundaries, including prompt injection.

children.name: Evaluation, benchmarking and data leakage
children.detail: Design representative tests, separate fitting from assessment, and measure quality, uncertainty, cost and failure modes.

children.name: Fairness, bias assessment and data governance
children.detail: Examine who benefits or bears errors, choose explicit fairness criteria, and document how data is collected and used.
